_about: Limits and the header list used by scripts/site_check.py. Every entry is dated. 'verified' is true only when the value was read in its source on the 'checked' date; false means it was written from memory and the script says so when it runs. Edit a level or a limit here, or pass --checks-file with your own copy.

certificate_fail_days.source: mstack default. No standard sets this; it is the point where a missed renewal becomes an outage within a week.

certificate_warn_days.source: mstack default. Automated renewal usually acts about 30 days before expiry, so less than this suggests renewal is not running.

hsts_min_max_age.source: About six months, the lower bound often advised for Strict-Transport-Security. Written from memory; read the current advice at developer.mozilla.org before relying on it.
hsts_min_max_age.note: working value; no primary source states a fixed number

redirect_hops_warn.source: mstack default. More than two redirects before a page is usually a configuration left over from a move.

headers.name: strict-transport-security
headers.why: without it a visitor's first request can be downgraded to plain http
headers.note: level is mstack's choice; the header itself is defined in the named standard

headers.name: x-content-type-options
headers.why: without 'nosniff' a browser may run a file as a type the server did not state
headers.source: WHATWG Fetch standard (nosniff); level chosen by mstack
headers.note: level is mstack's choice; the header itself is defined in the named standard

headers.name: content-security-policy
headers.why: limits where scripts, styles and frames may load from
headers.source: W3C Content Security Policy Level 3; level chosen by mstack
headers.note: level is mstack's choice; the header itself is defined in the named standard

headers.name: x-frame-options
headers.why: stops other sites showing the page inside a frame; frame-ancestors in the policy also counts
headers.source: RFC 7034 and CSP frame-ancestors; level chosen by mstack
headers.note: level is mstack's choice; the header itself is defined in the named standard

headers.name: referrer-policy
headers.why: controls how much of the address is sent to other sites
headers.source: W3C Referrer Policy; level chosen by mstack
headers.note: level is mstack's choice; the header itself is defined in the named standard

headers.name: permissions-policy
headers.why: switches off browser features the page does not use
headers.source: W3C Permissions Policy; level chosen by mstack
headers.note: level is mstack's choice; the header itself is defined in the named standard
